name: Warranty Vault
description: A receipt and warranty vault for the things you own — purchase dates, serial numbers, receipt photos, and a heads-up before each warranty runs out.

items.sql: SELECT id, name, category, purchase_date, price_cents, retailer, warranty_months, warranty_expires_date, serial_number, notes, receipt_file_id, receipt_doc_id, created_by, created_at, updated_at FROM app_warranty_vault__items

add_item.title: Track a warranty
add_item.description: Start tracking a purchase's warranty when another app's event fires — an appliance bought, a tool registered, equipment added elsewhere.

suggested_automations.title: Put each warranty's last day on the calendar
suggested_automations.description: When an item is added with a warranty, or its cover length is corrected, put the day the warranty runs out on the household calendar. A claim is only worth making while the cover still stands, and the calendar is where the household already looks. Editing the warranty later moves the entry that is already there instead of adding a second one.

suggested_automations.title: Take a warranty's last day back off the calendar
suggested_automations.description: The other half of the rule above, and it only does anything if you have that one. When an item is deleted, or its warranty is cleared, the calendar entry it put there stops showing — instead of standing forever as cover on something the household no longer owns. Add both, or the entry outlives the item.

source.query: SELECT id AS id, name AS title, NULLIF(retailer, '') AS subtitle, warranty_expires_date AS when_at FROM app_warranty_vault__items WHERE warranty_expires_date = :today ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 20

SELECT name AS title, category AS subtitle, warranty_expires_date AS expires_on FROM app_warranty_vault__items WHERE warranty_expires_date <> '' AND warranty_expires_date >= :today ORDER BY warranty_expires_date LIMIT 3
